The original problem A series of tasks has to be performed. These tasks can be complex and take up to 5 minutes to complete execution. But they're mostly I/O bound . The number of tasks to be performed can vary from 1-100,000. There can be 1-50 tasks being executed at the same time. The time that takes to execute a single task is all that matters in terms of performance. Each task has four types of outputs. Let's call them A, B, C and D. A and B can have size ranging from a few bytes up to 5 MB and each task could output 0-10,000 of each of them. C and D will be 1-5 KB in size and each task will assuredly output 10 of them each. These are to be output into 4 different queues. Current solution - async model Currently, each task is scheduled as a separate async task by a main process. Since everything runs in a single process, outputs can be easily shared to the main process from each async task. Everything just works. Issue with the async model There can be some sync blocking code in the task that is to be executed. This causes all the tasks to stop executing for that time.
